title: H. pylori stool test
what: This is a stool test. It looks for traces of a bacterium that lives in the stomach and can cause gastritis and ulcers.
why: For stomach pain or heaviness, heartburn, ulcers, stomach disease in relatives, or to check after treatment.
duration: collecting at home takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you took antibiotics in the last month
If you take medicines for heartburn or stomach acid
If you were already treated for H. pylori, and when you finished

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Antibiotics and acid medicines can change the result. Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide if a break is needed.

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Buy a sterile container with a small scoop at a pharmacy, or get one at the lab.

prepare.title: After treatment
prepare.text: A follow-up test is usually done at least 4 weeks after treatment ends. Your doctor will tell you when.

bring: The container with the stool sample
steps: Pass stool into a clean, dry pot or onto clean plastic wrap, not from the toilet bowl
Use the scoop in the lid to take a little stool
Close the container tightly and label it
Take it to the lab the same day
after: If you cannot take it right away, the container is usually kept in the fridge. Ask the lab how long
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when
If the bacterium is found, your doctor will prescribe treatment
red_flags: Black stools, or vomiting blood or something like coffee grounds: call emergency services

faq.q: Why a stool test instead of a blood test for H. pylori?
faq.a: Stool shows if the bacterium is there right now. Blood antibodies can stay after treatment.
Your doctor decides. Usually people with symptoms are tested.

reminders.text: H. pylori stool test tomorrow. Get the container and a clean pot ready.
